newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end down 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- prices end down 3/8.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended down 3/8 of a point Thursday, sympathizing with 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds' nearly full-point drop.
"In the municipal market it's different," one trader said. "No one makes adjustments when they are supposed to."
While muni cash should be down 1/2, "they are not trading anything down 1/2, but maybe 3/8 of a point," the trader said.
Action was light and bid lists were few, he said, with players reluctant to sell because replacements are hard to find.
"Plus, the account base has money to spend," the trader said. "They're just playing a waiting game."
A municipal analyst said the overall market ended down 3/8 of a point. High-grade issues worsened by two to three basis points, while dollar bonds were down 3/8 point.

Week to week, Reuters 10-year tax-exempt general obligation bond index fell to 4.83 percent Thursday, down from 4.89 percent the previous Thursday. This week's level is the lowest since the 4.82 percent posted December 5.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year closed down 31/32 at 99-22/32 to yield 6.65 percent. In debt futures, the March municipal contract closed down 17/32 at 117-7/32. The March T-bond contract closed down 19/32 at 113-1/32. The MOB spread was 134 ticks.
Turning new issues, competitive action saw Goldman Sachs & Co win $65.5 million Arlington Independent School District, Texas, school bonds at a net interest cost of 5.185 percent.
Also Thursday, Lehman Brothers said it won $56 million Virginia Public School Authority notes at a true interest cost of 4.171 percent.
"That deal was very clean," a source familiar with the offering said. "Everything is away."

As for next week's new deals, at least five negotiated offerings totaling $150 million or more are expected. Morgan Stanley & Co is expected to price $490 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corp bonds.
Goldman Sachs is expected to price $260 million New York State Thruway Authority bonds, while Smith Barney Inc is set to bring a $250 million Cook County, Ill., deal.
Also next week, Smith Barney is expected to price $250 million San Diego Public Facilities Financial Authority, Calif, bonds and $150 million Platte River Power Authority, Colo., bonds.
